message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"a71bffb988a4728035ef150ebd78650622714ec333e86edaedd16094a60db079","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nv-class-c:lineage:58","source_registry_sha256":"3e184808e042e052d0c78d0dff47c50b34a56560f428649c492afe10bc7ba712","units":[{"unit_id":"sec09-u01","module_id":"sec09-m01","objective_ids":["sec09-u01"],"title":{"text":"Trucks, buses and no-zones","fact_ids":["sec09-R01","sec09-F01","sec09-F02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Most crashes between large trucks and smaller cars are caused by the car drivers, and the people in the cars are far more likely to be hurt.","fact_ids":["sec09-F02","sec09-R01"]},{"text":"Trucks and buses have large blind spots and need far more room to stop, so where you drive around them matters.","fact_ids":["sec09-F03","sec09-F06"]},{"text":"Trucks and buses swing wide to turn, which makes the right-side no-zone doubly dangerous.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"A driver finishes passing a large truck on the freeway and wants to move back into its lane.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07"]},"reasoning":{"text":"After passing a truck or bus, wait until its whole front shows in your rearview mirror before moving into its lane, and then do not slow down.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F06"]},"result":{"text":"The driver waits for the truck's whole front to appear in the mirror, moves over, and keeps speed.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a truck driver can see you whenever you can see the truck.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05","sec09-F03"]},"correction":{"text":"If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, the driver cannot see you.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"No face in the mirror, no driver sees you.","fact_ids":["sec09-F05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A truck ahead swings wide to the left before turning right, leaving space by the curb. What should you do?","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},"answer":{"text":"Stay back and never squeeze between the truck and the curb.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"Trucks and buses may swing wide left to make a right turn, and the right-side no-zone is doubly dangerous, so never try to squeeze between one and the curb.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Sharing the road with trucks","fact_ids":["sec09-R01","sec09-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"How big vehicles differ.","fact_ids":["sec09-R01","sec09-F02"]},{"text":"The no-zones.","fact_ids":["sec09-R01","sec09-F02"]},{"text":"Passing and turning.","fact_ids":["sec09-R01","sec09-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson opens the chapter on sharing the road with large trucks and buses. The handbook puts crashes between cars and commercial vehicles at more than two hundred thousand a year, many of them avoidable. Most crashes between large trucks and smaller cars are caused by the car drivers, and the people in the cars are far more likely to be killed or hurt. We will cover how large vehicles differ from cars, the blind spots called no-zones, passing and following trucks safely, trucks backing up, and wide turns. The car driver has the most to gain from these rules.","fact_ids":["sec09-R01","sec09-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"How large vehicles differ","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Cannot maneuver like cars.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02"]},{"text":"Much bigger blind spots.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02"]},{"text":"Need more time and space to stop.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Large commercial vehicles cannot maneuver like cars, have much bigger blind spots, and need more time and space to slow down or stop. Large trucks and buses need nearly twice the time and distance cars need to stop, so cutting in front and slowing can get you rear-ended. Most crashes between large trucks and smaller cars are caused by the car drivers, and the people in the cars are far more likely to be killed or hurt. So the car driver has the most to gain from giving trucks room. Large vehicles need much more room than cars to slow down or stop.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The no-zones","fact_ids":["sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Blind spots at sides, rear and front.","fact_ids":["sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05"]},{"text":"Right side is doubly dangerous.","fact_ids":["sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05"]},{"text":"No face in the mirror, no view.","fact_ids":["sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"The no-zone is the set of blind spots around a large truck or bus, at its sides, rear and front, where a car effectively disappears from the driver's view. The right-side no-zone is doubly dangerous because trucks and buses swing wide when turning right. Do not linger beside a truck or bus: if you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, the driver cannot see you. Remember the three zones by position: beside the truck, directly behind it, and just in front of it. In all three, the truck driver may not know your car is there, so do not linger in any of them longer than you must when passing.","fact_ids":["sec09-F03","sec09-F04","sec09-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Passing and following","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wait for the whole front in your mirror.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F06"]},{"text":"Do not slow after moving in.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F06"]},{"text":"Do not tailgate.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"After passing a truck or bus, wait until its whole front shows in your rearview mirror before moving into its lane, and then do not slow down. Do not tailgate a truck or bus: its driver cannot see you directly behind, you cannot see the road beyond it, and a sudden stop leaves you nowhere to go. Large trucks and buses need nearly twice the time and distance cars need to stop, which is why cutting in front and slowing can get you rear-ended by one. The rear no-zone sits directly behind the truck, where its driver cannot see you and you cannot see past it.","fact_ids":["sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Backing and wide turns","fact_ids":["sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Never pass behind a backing truck.","fact_ids":["sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},{"text":"Trucks swing wide to turn.","fact_ids":["sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},{"text":"Never squeeze by the curb.","fact_ids":["sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Never pass behind a commercial truck that is backing up, because its driver cannot see vehicles or people directly behind it. Trucks and buses may swing wide left to make a right turn, or wide right to make a left turn, so never try to squeeze between one and the curb. Wait behind a backing truck until it has finished, because its driver cannot see what is directly behind it. When a truck or bus starts a turn by swinging wide, give it the room it needs and stay back from the curb side until the turn is complete. The right-side no-zone is doubly dangerous because of those wide right turns.","fact_ids":["sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Front versus rear no-zone","fact_ids":["sec09-R02","sec09-F06","sec09-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Front: cutting in and slowing.","fact_ids":["sec09-R02","sec09-F06","sec09-F08"]},{"text":"Rear: tailgating.","fact_ids":["sec09-R02","sec09-F06","sec09-F08"]},{"text":"Both: the driver cannot see you.","fact_ids":["sec09-R02","sec09-F06","sec09-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap with two no-zones. In the front no-zone the danger is cutting in too soon and slowing, which can get you rear-ended, because a large truck needs nearly twice the distance to stop. In the rear no-zone the danger is tailgating, where neither driver can see the other's situation. So the two mistakes are opposite: one is getting too close in front, the other too close behind. When a question describes a car just ahead of a truck, think about cutting in; when it describes a car behind, think about tailgating. Give trucks room in front and behind.","fact_ids":["sec09-R02","sec09-F06","sec09-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check a wide turn","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"A truck swings wide left.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},{"text":"It is turning right.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},{"text":"Space opens by the curb.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a truck ahead of you swings wide to the left before turning right, leaving space by the curb. What should you do? Decide before reading on. Stay back and never squeeze between the truck and the curb. Trucks and buses may swing wide left to make a right turn, and the right-side no-zone is doubly dangerous because of those wide right turns. Large trucks and buses also have much bigger blind spots than cars, and the right-side no-zone is the one beside the curb. Give the truck room, let it finish the turn, and only then continue past the corner yourself.","fact_ids":["sec09-F10","sec09-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u01-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Trucks recap","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Give trucks room.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-R02"]},{"text":"See the driver's face.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-R02"]},{"text":"No squeezing, no tailgating.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"To review, large commercial vehicles cannot maneuver like cars, have much bigger blind spots and need nearly twice the time and distance to stop, and car drivers cause most car-truck crashes. The no-zones are the blind spots at a truck's sides, rear and front; if you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you. After passing, wait for the truck's whole front in your mirror, then keep your speed. Do not tailgate, never pass behind a backing truck, and never squeeze between a wide-turning truck and the curb. Remember the right-side no-zone.","fact_ids":["sec09-F01","sec09-F06","sec09-F02","sec09-F03","sec09-F05","sec09-F07","sec09-F08","sec09-F09","sec09-F10","sec09-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec09-u02","module_id":"sec09-m02","objective_ids":["sec09-u02"],"title":{"text":"Motorcycles and mopeds","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Motorcyclists have the same rights as other drivers, but motorcycles are harder to see and judge.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F13"]},{"text":"Mopeds have their own limits and lane rules in Nevada.","fact_ids":["sec09-F19","sec09-F20"]},{"text":"Headlight glare is especially dangerous to riders who steer by balance.","fact_ids":["sec09-F16"]},{"text":"Lane sharing between motorcycles is allowed only with the riders’ consent.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"At night, a driver comes up behind a motorcycle with high beams on.","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F15"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle, and begin slowing earlier than for a car while keeping a generous gap.","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F15"]},"result":{"text":"The driver dims the headlights, slows early and keeps a generous gap behind the rider.","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F15"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: assuming a motorcycle's blinking turn signal means the rider is about to turn.","fact_ids":["sec09-F14"]},"correction":{"text":"Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so be sure what the rider is actually doing before you move.","fact_ids":["sec09-F14","sec09-R03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Dim, slow early, leave room.","fact_ids":["sec09-F16","sec09-F15"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Two motorcyclists want to ride side by side in one lane. When is that allowed?","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]},"answer":{"text":"Only with the drivers' consent, and no more than two abreast.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"With the drivers' consent, motorcycles and mopeds may ride at most two abreast in one lane; without consent they must ride staggered.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Riders on two wheels","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Motorcyclists' rights.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F13"]},{"text":"Why they are hard to judge.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F13"]},{"text":"Moped rules.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers sharing the road with motorcycles and mopeds. Motorcyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers, including the right to use a full traffic lane. But motorcycles are small, so they are harder to see, may seem farther away than they really are, and their speed is hard to judge. We will look at lane sharing, rider clues, following and dimming rules, the endorsement riders need, and the special limits Nevada sets for mopeds, including their lane rule, registration and helmets. Watch for them closely.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Rights and lane sharing","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"A full lane for every rider.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F18"]},{"text":"Two abreast only with consent.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F18"]},{"text":"Otherwise staggered.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"Motorcyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers, including the right to use a full traffic lane. With the drivers' consent, motorcycles and mopeds may ride at most two abreast in a single lane; without consent they must ride staggered. Riding a motorcycle requires a special endorsement on a Nevada driver's license. A motorcyclist has the same rights and responsibilities as any other driver on the road. Two riders sharing one lane is allowed only when both agree, and never more than two side by side; without that consent, they ride staggered. Riding a motorcycle also requires a special endorsement on a Nevada driver's license.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F18"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Seeing and reading riders","fact_ids":["sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Harder to see; seem farther away.","fact_ids":["sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04"]},{"text":"Signals may not cancel.","fact_ids":["sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04"]},{"text":"Watch head turns and leaning.","fact_ids":["sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Motorcycles are small, so they are harder to see, may seem farther away than they really are, and their speed is hard to judge. Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so before a turn or lane change that depends on a rider's path, be sure what the rider is actually doing. Clues to a motorcyclist's next move include the rider or passenger turning their head to look back and the rider starting to lean or tilt the motorcycle. Strong winds or a rough road surface can push a motorcycle out of its position on the road. Look twice before you move.","fact_ids":["sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Following a motorcycle","fact_ids":["sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Slow earlier than for a car.","fact_ids":["sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},{"text":"Keep a generous gap.","fact_ids":["sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},{"text":"Dim headlights; more room in rain.","fact_ids":["sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Approaching a motorcycle from behind, begin slowing earlier than you would for a car and keep a generous gap. Always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle, because riders steer by balance and high-beam glare is more dangerous to them than to car or truck drivers. Leave even more following distance behind a motorcycle when it is raining or the road is slippery. Riders steer by balance, which is why high-beam glare is more dangerous to them, and the handbook asks for even more following distance when it is raining or the road is slippery. Slowing earlier, keeping a generous gap and dimming your lights are the three habits to use every time you come up behind a motorcycle.","fact_ids":["sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":48,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Mopeds","fact_ids":["sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Limited power and top speed.","fact_ids":["sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Far right lane in most cases.","fact_ids":["sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Registered, uninsured, helmets on.","fact_ids":["sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Nevada sets a moped apart by motor size, a maximum of two brake horsepower, and a top speed of thirty miles per hour on flat or nearly flat ground. Moped riders must stay in the far right lane unless there is only one lane, they are preparing a left turn within a quarter mile, the right lane is unsafe, or a police officer directs otherwise. Mopeds must be registered with the DMV for a one-time fee but need no insurance, and moped riders and passengers must wear helmets. Drivers around mopeds take the same precautions as around motorcycles.","fact_ids":["sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Motorcycle or moped?","fact_ids":["sec09-R05","sec09-F18","sec09-F20","sec09-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Motorcycles need an endorsement.","fact_ids":["sec09-R05","sec09-F18","sec09-F20","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Mopeds keep to the far right.","fact_ids":["sec09-R05","sec09-F18","sec09-F20","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Both get the same care.","fact_ids":["sec09-R05","sec09-F18","sec09-F20","sec09-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap with two kinds of two-wheelers. Motorcycles need a license endorsement, while mopeds, limited in horsepower and to a top speed of thirty miles per hour, must keep to the far right lane in most situations. So the endorsement belongs to the motorcycle, and the far-right lane rule belongs to the moped. What they share is the care drivers must give them: the same precautions apply around mopeds as around motorcycles, and moped riders have the same rights and duties as other drivers, plus extra ones tied to their limits. Give both kinds of riders room.","fact_ids":["sec09-R05","sec09-F18","sec09-F20","sec09-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check lane sharing","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two riders, one lane.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-F11"]},{"text":"When is it allowed?","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: two motorcyclists want to ride side by side in one lane. When is that allowed? Recall the rule before reading on. It is allowed only with the drivers' consent, and no more than two may ride abreast in a single lane. Without consent, they must ride in a staggered formation. The same rule applies to mopeds. A single motorcyclist has the right to use the full traffic lane. Motorcycles are small, may seem farther away than they really are, and their speed is hard to judge, so give every rider plenty of room, whether one is riding alone or two are riding abreast with consent.","fact_ids":["sec09-F12","sec09-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec09-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Two-wheelers recap","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17","sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R05","sec09-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Full lane; two abreast with consent.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17","sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R05","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Dim, slow early, leave room.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17","sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R05","sec09-R08"]},{"text":"Mopeds keep right.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17","sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R05","sec09-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, motorcyclists have full rights to a lane, and two may ride abreast only with consent. Motorcycles are hard to see and judge, their signals may not cancel, and head turns or leaning show a rider's next move; wind and rough roads can push them off line. Slow earlier behind a motorcycle, keep a generous gap, dim your headlights and leave more room in the rain. Motorcycles need an endorsement. Mopeds are limited in power and speed, keep to the far right in most cases, are registered without insurance, and their riders wear helmets. Give them room.","fact_ids":["sec09-F11","sec09-F12","sec09-F13","sec09-F14","sec09-R03","sec09-R04","sec09-F15","sec09-F16","sec09-F17","sec09-F18","sec09-F19","sec09-F20","sec09-F21","sec09-R05","sec09-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec09-u03","module_id":"sec09-m03","objective_ids":["sec09-u03"],"title":{"text":"School buses and truck beds","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F23","sec09-R06"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Stopping for school buses protects children getting on and off, and the rule applies almost everywhere.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]},{"text":"Young riders are kept out of truck beds on paved highways.","fact_ids":["sec09-F29"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"On a divided highway, a driver going the opposite way sees a school bus stopped with flashing red lights.","fact_ids":["sec09-F23","sec09-R06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"On a divided highway, you must stop for a school bus only when traveling in the same direction as the bus.","fact_ids":["sec09-F23","sec09-R06"]},"result":{"text":"This driver, traveling the opposite way on a divided highway, does not have to stop.","fact_ids":["sec09-F23"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking drivers on the other side of any road may keep going past a stopped school bus.","fact_ids":["sec09-R06"]},"correction":{"text":"On an undivided road, traffic in both directions stops for a school bus with flashing red lights.","fact_ids":["sec09-R06","sec09-F22"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Red lights flashing, everyone stops, except across a divider.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F23"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A school bus with flashing red lights has stopped. When may you go past it?","fact_ids":["sec09-F22"]},"answer":{"text":"Only after the bus driver turns the flashing red lights off.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22"]},"rationale":{"text":"You must stop for a school bus showing a flashing red signal and may not pass until the driver turns those lights off.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec09-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Children on and off buses","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F29"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stopping for school buses.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F29"]},{"text":"The divided-highway rule.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F29"]},{"text":"Riding in truck beds.","fact_ids":["sec09-F22","sec09-F29"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers two rules that protect young people. You must stop at any location for a school bus showing a flashing red signal, and you may not pass it until the bus driver turns those lights off.
